title: Compute for-loop elements of a colon range arithmetically
motivation: A `for` loop over a scalar `:` range read each element from the range vector with `_seq[[idx]]` (`Fir_subscript_read_int` in C), and for a compact `1:n` that read is an ALTREP method call. The value is only `from + idx` or `from - idx`, so each trip paid a vector access for a value that two registers already give. permute_fake, permute, queens, sieve and vector_for showed the cost; for example permute_fake had 10 such reads and queens 25.
solution: The new pass `ElideRangeRead` runs in the main fixpoint after `ElideRedundantBoxUnbox`. It matches the loop shape that bc2fir gives over a static `:` call on two scalars whose result is known to be an integer vector, proves that the read is in bounds, and replaces the read with a call of the new intrinsic `rangeElement(from, k, step)`, which is `from + (k - 1) * step` with a `step` of 1 or -1. The intrinsic has no `@signals` mark, because an element in bounds cannot overflow. So `Cleanup` can remove an unused element. It keeps an unused integer `-`, `*` or `+`, because they can warn. The pass removes a read whose value is unused, and also the index decrement `idx = k - 1` if nothing else uses it. Then the C compiler folds a loop that does nothing. If the direction is not constant, a new block on the loop's entry edge tests `from <= to` once. The `:` allocation and `length` stay, because the `:` result is on the deopt stack of its checkpoint. Also in this range: a bc2fir fix that steps the `for` loop index with the new intrinsic `forIndex`, which gives `NA` after `INT_MAX` without the overflow warning of `+`, and ends the loop when the index is `NA` (`naToTrue`); the pass matches this step, and an `OptimizeCallee` fix that keeps an intrinsic call such as `toForSeq` static.

files.client/rsh/src/fir2c/runtime_inline.h: Adds the inline `forIndex` intrinsic (`Fir_for_index`), which gives `NA` for `NA` and past `INT_MAX`, and the inline `rangeElement` intrinsic. Both compute in `int64_t`.
files.repo-map.md: Adds the lines for `ElideRangeRead.java`, `ForLoopTest.java`, and the examples `for_colon_ranges.R` and `for_colon_nan_error.R`.
files.server/src/main/java/org/prlprg/bc2fir/B: The `for` step block computes the index with `forIndex` in place of `+` and tests `naToTrue(len < k)` in place of `naToFalse`, so the loop ends after `INT_MAX` trips.
files.server/src/main/java/org/prlprg/fir/inte: Registers the boxed and unboxed `forIndex` and the unboxed `rangeElement` in the FIŘ interpreter.
files.server/src/main/java/org/prlprg/fir/opt/: New pass that matches the `forIndex` step of a `for` loop, replaces its element read of a scalar `:` range with `rangeElement(from, k, step)`, and removes the dead index decrement.
Adds `ElideRangeRead` to the main fixpoint, after `ElideRedundantBoxUnbox` and before `SchedulePure`.
A call to an intrinsic never becomes a dispatch, also when a better version could run.
files.server/src/main/resources/org/prlprg/fir: Declares the intrinsic `forIndex` with a boxed and an unboxed integer version, and the intrinsic `rangeElement` with an unboxed integer version.
files.server/src/test/java/org/prlprg/bc2fir/F: New test that the `for` loop of bc2fir steps its index with `forIndex` and uses `naToTrue` for its exit test.
files.server/src/test/java/org/prlprg/fir/opt/: New tests for integer, real and constant ranges, inner loops, dead reads, and a dead element that `Cleanup` removes with its index decrement and direction test, and for shapes the pass must leave alone.
New test that a `toForSeq` intrinsic call stays static when a better version could run.
files.server/src/test/resources/org/prlprg/exa: New example whose `for` loop over `a:NaN` must give GNU-R's error, not a descending loop.
New example with `for` loops over `a:b` that count up, down, once, or from a real bound, and nested ranges.
